title: Connect ZEAL's partner handoff across Pipedrive, Make, Airtable and ClickUp

facts: Upwork post: Senior AI Automation & Systems Architect: Make, Airtable, ClickUp, APIs (ZEAL travel marketplace, Milestone 1 internal operating system).
Stack named in the post: ClickUp, Make.com, Airtable, Pipedrive, OpenAI API, BigQuery, Sigma, Amplitude, Google Workspace, Slack.
Milestone 1 asks: consistent data models, record identifiers, source-of-truth rules, automated handoffs, error handling, monitoring, logging and documentation.
Personalization: Eric named in two separate client reviews (2024-02-28 and 2022-11-28).

cover.beat: This is the first piece of {{client.name}}'s operating system. When a partner deal is signed in Pipedrive, it becomes one Airtable record and an assigned ClickUp task, without anyone copying data between tools.

scenes.title: Here's how your tools connect for Milestone 1.
scenes.caption: Each tool owns one job, and one partner ID ties them together.
scenes.beat: Pipedrive owns the deal, Airtable owns the partner record, and ClickUp owns the work. Make sits in the middle and moves the data. Every partner gets one ID, {{partner.zealId}}, and that ID is how each tool finds the same partner.

scenes.title: Follow one signed partner through Make.
scenes.caption: Make looks for the partner ID before it creates anything.
scenes.beat: The signed deal comes into Make. Before it creates anything, it searches Airtable for {{partner.zealId}}. This is a new partner, so it creates the record, writes the summary, opens the ClickUp task for {{owner.name}} and posts the handoff. If the partner already existed, the same record gets updated instead. If the ID is missing, ops gets an alert.
details: Repeat deliveries take the update route, so no second record
HTTP request modules stand in for the Airtable, OpenAI and ClickUp calls; field IDs are set during the build
